solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Round, soft, shapeless mass

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical marking for playing softly
a lump is a mass with no particular shape

explanation.surface: A description of some dough or clay: round, soft and without form.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump describes something rounded and well filled out, a synonym for round in that sense.

clue.text: Turn on to drink Irish drink

indicators.note: turn says the words that follow are spun round to read backwards

parts.note: a nip is a small drink

explanation.surface: Someone is persuaded to have an Irish drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' reverses ON TO NIP to give PINOTNO.
explanation.definitionFit: A red wine made from the Burgundian grape of that name is a drink.

clue.text: Single from Upper Norwood was extremely dear, initially

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A single person in Upper Norwood, a south London district, found life very expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwed means not married, which is single.

clue.text: Fizzy drink and cheesy stuff for snack

parts.note: pop is a fizzy soft drink
corn is hackneyed, sentimental material

explanation.surface: A soda and some cheese as a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheesy' is not about cheese but means trite.
explanation.definitionFit: Popped maize kernels are a snack food eaten at the cinema.

clue.text: Character excellent in hearing, this impairing vision?

indicators.note: in hearing says the letters are what the spoken words sound like

parts.note: a character is a letter, here P, and excellent is super; said together they make the phrase

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about an excellent character, then a question about something that spoils one's sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter P is pronounced PEA and SUPER can be said SOUPER, so the two together sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense yellowish London smog, thick as pea soup, was so named because it made seeing almost impossible.

clue.text: Particular girl having lost head, breaking nose

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open the other word to sit inside it

parts.note: to nose is to pry

indicators.note: having lost head means the first letter goes

parts.note: a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: A fussy girl, decapitated, smashing someone's nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost head' takes M off MISS, leaving ISS to break into PRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fussy and over-fastidious is being prissy.

clue.text: Area isn't for development as well

indicators.note: for development says the letters are worked into something new

explanation.surface: A plot of land not earmarked for building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as well' reads as 'also' but is the definition: an artesian well.
explanation.definitionFit: An artesian well is one where pressure forces water up, so the word describes a type of well.

clue.text: How to bowl — very unusual spins in order

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the order

parts.note: the OM is the Order of Merit

indicators.note: spins says the word turns round to read backwards

parts.note: rare means unusual

explanation.surface: Cricket advice: a very unusual bowler spins the ball properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spins' reverses RARE to ERAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowling with the arm swung over the shoulder is the standard cricket delivery style.

clue.text: Transpose letters for female supporter?

indicators.note: Transpose letters is an instruction to rearrange the letters of the word

explanation.surface: An instruction to swap the letters around.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who sponsors or backs a cause is a supporter, the feminine of patron.

clue.text: Fit to study psychology in the end

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

indicators.note: in the end picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone fit to study psychology after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready means prepared, which is fit as in fit for duty.

clue.text: Stories written on this modern race

parts.note: new means modern
a sprint is a short fast race

explanation.surface: Tales printed about a contemporary running event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stories' reads as part of the wordplay, but the definition is the whole opening phrase: what news stories are printed on.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap paper used for newspapers is the material on which reports are printed.

clue.text: More old pictures recalled

parts.note: ex- is a prefix meaning former or old

indicators.note: recalled, called back, says the word for pictures is read in the other direction

parts.note: pictures collectively are art

explanation.surface: Someone wants more old photographs brought back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' looks like remembering, but it signals the pictures word read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, so it works as a synonym for more.

clue.text: Exhausting, when outside in a storm

indicators.note: in a storm suggests things tossed about wildly, so the letters of the next word are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Being outdoors during a storm is exhausting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a storm' rearranges OUTSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tedious is wearisome and tiring, so exhausting in the sense of draining.

clue.text: Notice loud clothes, being dark and mysterious

indicators.note: clothes means wraps around, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: loud colours or clothes are showy
an ad, advertisement, is a public notice

explanation.surface: Someone notices garish clothes on a dark, mysterious figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun for garments, but it is a verb meaning wraps around; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadowy means obscure and hard to make out, as in a shadowy figure of uncertain identity.

clue.text: Those known as vegetables

parts.note: the idiom 'to know your ...' means to know your subject well, so these are the vegetables people know

explanation.surface: A list of vegetables by name.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'know your onions' means to be expert in something.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition built on the idiom of being knowledgeable, the bulb vegetables one is said to know.

clue.text: Constant sent in as variable divided by constant

indicators.note: divided by means split apart by another letter placed within
variable means changeable, so these letters change their order

parts.note: c is a symbol for a constant in mathematics

explanation.surface: Mathematical jargon: something sent in as a variable divided by a constant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variable' rearranges SENT IN AS, then C goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Incessant means never ceasing, a synonym for continual or constant.

clue.text: Inoffensive home front, incapable of attacking?

indicators.note: front means the first letter of the word that precedes it

parts.note: without arms, so with no weapons to attack with

explanation.surface: A wartime home front that could not mount any attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home front' looks like one wartime phrase; it is the first letter of home.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmless means doing no harm, a synonym for inoffensive.

clue.text: A half a frippery

definitions.meaning: a half pint of weak beer

explanation.surface: Half of something trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: A half is a British pub order of half a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally weak beer, the phrase also means something of no importance.

clue.text: Death kept in check, that's appreciated in feud

indicators.note: kept in means held inside another piece

parts.note: to vet is to check
end means death
ta is a British informal thank you

explanation.surface: A death held in check in a feud, with gratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a long-running blood feud between families.

clue.text: Bouncer's firm punching outrageous, then the fight ends

indicators.note: punching means driving into, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: rich, as in 'that's a bit rich', means outrageous
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: ends means the final letters of the two words named

explanation.surface: A nightclub bouncer's firm hits someone outrageously before the brawl stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' suggests a doorman, but it is something that bounces off a surface; 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ricochet is a projectile that rebounds off a surface, so a thing that bounces.

clue.text: Person who solves a beauty?

explanation.surface: Someone who solves a lovely puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a codebreaker and informal praise for something excellent.

clue.text: Plant fool among those working in intelligence

indicators.note: among puts the fool in the middle of the agency

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A spy plants an idiot among the intelligence officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' hints at an undercover agent, but it is botanical.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassia is a genus of shrubs and trees, including one whose bark is used like cinnamon.

clue.text: Same sad set assembled

indicators.note: set means arranged, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: The same miserable group gathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Amassed means gathered together, a synonym for assembled.

clue.text: Honest, old-fashioned figure

definitions.meaning: a person out of touch and conventional, or a four-sided shape

explanation.surface: An honest person of the old school.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means fair and honest, and also a stuffy conventional person or a geometric figure.

clue.text: Something bright in something dark yellow

indicators.note: in places one thing within the other

parts.note: mud is dark muddy earth
a star is a bright object in the sky

explanation.surface: A puzzle about something bright inside something dark yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dark yellow' reads as one colour, but 'dark' belongs to the wordplay and 'yellow' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustard is a shade of yellow, named after the condiment's colour.

clue.text: Master bird call, as a parrot

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts
caw is the call of a crow

explanation.surface: Learning to mimic a bird call as a parrot does.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaw is a large brightly coloured South American parrot.

clue.text: Missile controversy

definitions.meaning: a crossbow bolt with a square head, a projectile

explanation.surface: A row about a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a square-headed crossbow bolt and a heated argument.

clue.text: Brown pan

definitions.meaning: cook in an oven so as to brown it

explanation.surface: A brown cooking pan.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to cook by browning in an oven and to criticise severely.

clue.text: Device for turning nut

definitions.meaning: a handle on a shaft used to turn an engine or mechanism
an eccentric person, a nut case

explanation.surface: A mechanism that turns a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nut' looks like the hardware a device turns, but it means an eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a bent handle for rotating a shaft and an oddball.

clue.text: Explain why railway customers dissatisfied, one getting lost?

indicators.note: getting lost says that letter goes missing from the phrase

parts.note: late trains are why rail passengers are unhappy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Account for the grumbling of rail passengers, one of whom has lost their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting lost' drops I from TRAINS LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To translate is to put into plainer words, a synonym for explain.

clue.text: Lock exit for president?

definitions.meaning: a ... is a sluice or canal lock gate
the scandal that forced President Nixon to resign

explanation.surface: A locked door as an escape route for a president.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words it is a lock gate; capitalised it is the 1970s scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1972 break-in scandal led to Nixon's resignation, while the plain words name a floodgate.

clue.text: Stop some trade, terminated

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Halt some business that has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage or prevent, so to stop someone acting.
